The clinical record provides strong evidence for sarcoidosis, including non-caseating microgranulomas in biopsies from multiple gastrointestinal sites (stomach, duodenum, terminal ileum, colon, rectum) and an elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level. Other potential causes of granulomas were ruled out (e.g., infections, Crohn's disease).

The record explicitly states 'duodenitis' was found on EGD and biopsies from the duodenum showed non-caseating microgranulomas. This duodenitis is a manifestation or component of the broader sarcoidosis diagnosis, not the complete diagnosis itself.

candidate_relations.reason: While the patient has GI symptoms and inflammation, the presence of non-caseating microgranulomas in multiple organs (GI tract, elevated ACE suggesting systemic involvement) points strongly to sarcoidosis rather than inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Although Crohn's disease (a type of IBD) can have granulomas, the widespread nature and elevated ACE make sarcoidosis a more fitting overarching diagnosis, and other IBD features are not specifically highlighted as primary.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Inflammatory bowel disease vs. Sarcoidosis with GI involvement
